For Becky & Kit · July 24 – August 2, 2026

Argentina.

Five nights in Buenos Aires, two beside the falls in Iguazú, bookended by overnight flights from San Diego. The pace is unhurried, the lodging is hand-picked for sleep and atmosphere, and the days build around the Buenos Aires that travelers in the know come back for: independent theater, contemporary art, leafy gardens, an English-led tour through a 1919 theater-turned-bookstore.

Depart San DiegoFriday, July 24 · evening
Return San DiegoSunday, August 2 · morning
Buenos Aires5 nights · Palo Santo Hotel · Palermo Hollywood
Iguazú Falls2 nights · Loi Suites · Iryapú jungle

The journey, day by day

Travel
Friday, July 24 · leaving San Diego

Evening departure from SAN — connect at Dallas, then the overnight to Buenos Aires (EZE). You sleep through the cabin lights and wake somewhere over Brazil. The 24th and 25th collapse into one long arc of flying.

Day 1
Saturday, July 25 · bienvenidos a Buenos Aires

Land EZE in the morning, after the overnight from Dallas. Slip through customs and settle into Palo Santo Hotel — a 26-room boutique in Palermo Hollywood, draped in vertical gardens. Lunch on a leafy side street. A long walk through the neighborhood. An early Argentine dinner.

Day 2
Sunday, July 26 · gardens and modern art

A quiet morning in the Jardín Botánico Carlos Thays, the 1890s gardens designed by the French landscape architect. After lunch, MALBA — the Museo de Arte Latinoamericano — for Frida Kahlo's Diego y yo and the most important Latin American collection on the continent.

Day 3
Monday, July 27 · Dante and a bookstore in a theater

A morning English-language tour of Palacio Barolo, the 1923 building designed around Dante's Divine Comedy, ending at the rooftop lighthouse. In the afternoon, a short ride to El Ateneo Grand Splendid in Recoleta — the 1919 grand theater reborn as a bookstore, with frescoed ceilings and reading nooks where the opera boxes used to be.

Day 4
Tuesday, July 28 · Recoleta in full

The 11 AM English tour of Recoleta Cemetery, then lunch in the neighborhood, then the National Fine Arts Museum (Goya, Rodin, Monet, Argentine masters — and free). Late afternoon along the Reserva Ecológica Costanera Sur, the river-edge wetland.

Day 5
Wednesday, July 29 · Buenos Aires at your own pace

A solo morning for each — coffee, a bookshop, a long Palermo wander. In the afternoon, the English-language tour of Teatro Colón, one of the five great opera houses of the world. Dinner, then the night at Casa Brandon, the queer cultural center named for Brandon Teena — film, books, art, a small bar. Optional late drop-in at Mundo Lingo, the multilingual social where conversation starts by the flag on your name tag.

Day 6
Thursday, July 30 · north to the jungle

Morning flight to Iguazú. Loi Suites is a five-star jungle resort, wooden walkways suspended over the rainforest, adults-only heated pool and full spa. An easy afternoon along the park's Lower Circuit — boardwalks and the first views of the falls.

Day 7
Friday, July 31 · Iguazú in full

The Upper Circuit's panoramic vistas, an optional zodiac boat ride into the spray, and Devil's Throat in the late afternoon when the day crowds clear — that's when the cascade is at its most cinematic.

Day 8
Saturday, August 1 · the slow morning, the long flight

A late breakfast at Loi Suites, then the midday flight to Buenos Aires (AEP), a quick transfer to Ezeiza (EZE), and the evening overnight back to Dallas. You spend the night in the air.

Travel
Sunday, August 2 · home

The overnight from Buenos Aires lands in Dallas at dawn; final connection puts you back in San Diego mid-morning. Plan a quiet Sunday — the time zones are kind on the way home (BA is only 4 hours ahead of SD), but the overnight is still an overnight.

Must-do this week

Lock the trip in. Everything else sequences out over the next six weeks.

  • Confirm both passports valid through February 2027 — renew now if close (routine processing is 6–8 weeks).
  • Book the flights — SAN → DFW → EZE on American, single ticket, premium economy or business class.
  • Reserve Palo Santo Hotel for July 25–30 — request an upper floor or garden-facing room.
  • Reserve Loi Suites Iguazú for July 30 – August 1 — arrange the airport transfer when booking.
  • Buy Argentine travel health insurance ($30K+ medical/evacuation, now required at entry).

Day-by-day in detail

Times, addresses, what to know.

Friday, July 24 · departure from San Diego

  • Evening flight SAN → DFW on American.
  • Connect in Dallas (target a ~3-hour layover — long enough to eat, short enough not to drag).
  • Overnight DFW → EZE on American (777 or 787). Lights out for most of the cabin.
  • You will not get a real night of sleep, even in business class — pack accordingly.

Saturday, July 25 · arrival in Buenos Aires

  • Land EZE in the morning. Uber to Palermo Hollywood (~45 min, ~$30–50). Walk past the unmarked-taxi touts to the official Uber pickup.
  • Check into Palo Santo Hotel (Bonpland 2275, Palermo Hollywood). Confirm the 21% VAT waiver at check-in with passports — applies when paying with a non-Argentine card.
  • Lunch nearby. Nap. Easy walk.
  • Early dinner, early bed.

Sunday, July 26 · gardens & MALBA

  • 9 AM Jardín Botánico Carlos Thays — Av. Santa Fe 3951, walkable from the hotel. Free entry, quietest at opening, two hours.
  • Lunch in Palermo.
  • MALBA — Av. Figueroa Alcorta 3415. Two to three hours. Closed Tuesdays, so Sunday is the slot.
  • Evening: Palermo dinner.

Monday, July 27 · Palacio Barolo & El Ateneo

  • Morning English tour of Palacio Barolo — Av. de Mayo 1370, Monserrat. Book the English-language tour specifically — only the English tour reaches the rooftop lighthouse. ~90 min.
  • Lunch in Microcentro or along Avenida de Mayo.
  • El Ateneo Grand Splendid — Av. Santa Fe 1860, Recoleta. ~15 min Uber from Microcentro. The "Grand Splendid Experience" launched January 2026 tells the building's history.
  • Evening: free.

Tuesday, July 28 · Recoleta day

  • 11 AM Recoleta Cemetery English tour — Junín 1760. ~$15/person foreigner admission. Tuesday/Thursday/Saturday English tours at 11 AM.
  • Lunch in Recoleta.
  • Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes — Av. del Libertador 1473, free, across from the cemetery. Two hours.
  • Late afternoon: Reserva Ecológica Costanera Sur — Puerto Madero. Open Tuesday (closed Mondays). ~20 min Uber from MNBA.
  • Evening: quiet dinner.

Wednesday, July 29 · solo morning, Colón, Casa Brandon

  • Morning unscheduled. Becky and Kit split. Coffee, a bookshop, a long Palermo wander.
  • Lunch.
  • Teatro Colón English tour — Cerrito 628. Book the 2 PM or 3 PM slot. Tickets release exactly 21 days ahead — set a calendar alarm for July 7.
  • Late afternoon: coffee back in Palermo.
  • 8 PM Casa Brandon — Luis María Drago 236, Villa Crespo. Programming posts ~2 weeks out; confirm at brandon.org.ar or DM Instagram around July 15.
  • Optional 9 PM drop-in at Mundo Lingo at Baum Catrina, Palermo Soho (Wednesday session — no booking, name-tags-by-flag).

Thursday, July 30 · north to Iguazú

  • Morning flight AEP → IGR on Aerolíneas Argentinas (~1h45m). Leave bulk luggage at Palo Santo if returning; the hotel will hold it.
  • Loi Suites pre-arranged transfer ($50/vehicle, arranged 48 hours ahead at booking).
  • Afternoon: Lower Circuit in Iguazú National Park — ~1.7 km of mostly-flat boardwalk, the gentle introduction.
  • Dinner at Loi Suites.

Friday, July 31 · Iguazú in full

  • Park opens 8 AM — arrive at opening.
  • Morning: Upper Circuit (~1.2 km, panoramic).
  • Optional: Gran Aventura zodiac boat ride under the falls. Bring a waterproof phone pouch.
  • Lunch.
  • Late afternoon: Devil's Throat by ecological train, around 3–4 PM as the bus crowds clear.
  • Evening: Loi Suites — pool, jungle walks, the adults-only heated pool.

Saturday, August 1 · last morning in Argentina, evening flight out

  • Slow morning at Loi Suites.
  • AR1777 11:00 IGR → AEP (or AR1779 12:45 if 11:00 unavailable).
  • Uber from AEP to EZE (60–90 minutes weekend afternoon).
  • Arrive EZE by ~3 PM for evening international flight.
  • Evening EZE → DFW overnight. You spend the night in the air.

Sunday, August 2 · arrive home in San Diego

  • Overnight EZE → DFW lands in Dallas around dawn.
  • Morning connection DFW → SAN on American.
  • Arrive San Diego mid-morning.
  • You will be tired. Plan nothing for Sunday afternoon.

Lodging

Palo Santo Hotel — Buenos Aires

  • Bonpland 2275, Palermo Hollywood
  • 4-star boutique · 26 rooms · Booking 9.3/10
  • Vertical gardens soften street sound; quiet by design.
  • Request at booking: upper floor or garden-facing room.
  • Pay with non-Argentine card to waive the 21% VAT — confirm at check-in with passport.
  • Sources: palosantohotel.com · Booking.com

Loi Suites Iguazú

  • Selva Iryapú s/n, Puerto Iguazú
  • 5-star jungle resort · wooden walkways through native rainforest · adults-only heated pool · full spa open until midnight
  • Captive for evening dining — plan two in-resort dinners.
  • $50/vehicle airport transfer, pre-arranged 48 hours ahead.
  • Sources: loisuites.com.ar · Booking.com

Flights

International — primary

SAN → DFW → EZE on American Airlines, single PNR, both directions. Connection at Dallas; overnight 777/787 to Buenos Aires. ~3-hour DFW layover is the sweet spot.

Note: American's summer EZE service ends August 3, 2026. Confirm the specific August 1 EZE → DFW flight is operating before purchase — and book this week.

International — alternates (if DFW sells out)

  • SAN → MIA → EZE on American — Miami is American's year-round EZE gateway.
  • SAN → ATL → EZE on Delta — Atlanta hub.
  • SAN → IAH → EZE on United — Houston hub.

Cabin

  • Premium Economy — the comfort floor for an overnight leg.
  • Business class — lie-flat seats, real sleep on the overnight.

Domestic — Buenos Aires ⇄ Iguazú

  • Aerolíneas Argentinas (the only carrier on this route).
  • Outbound: AEP → IGR Thursday July 30, morning.
  • Return: AR1777 11:00 IGR → AEP Saturday August 1 (or AR1779 12:45). Earlier is safer.

AEP and EZE are different airports. Domestic uses Aeroparque (AEP), in the city. International uses Ezeiza (EZE), 45 minutes south. The Saturday transfer between them takes 60–90 minutes; budget 3+ hours total from AEP arrival to EZE international check-in.

Practical

Passport & entry

US citizens don't need a tourist visa for Argentina (≤90 days). Passport valid 6+ months past entry. Argentine health insurance ($30K+ medical / evacuation) is now required and may be asked for at check-in.

Money

21% VAT on hotel stays is waived for foreign tourists paying with a non-Argentine card. Argentina's foreign-exchange controls were lifted in April 2025; all rates are now within ~3% of each other. Foreign Visa or Mastercard at the MEP rate is now the simple winner for nearly everything. Bring ~$100–150 USD cash for tips and the smallest vendors.

Weather — Argentine winter

Buenos Aires: highs 12–15°C, lows 5–8°C, often damp. Warm coat, layers, rain jacket, sturdy walking shoes.

Iguazú: highs 20–23°C, lows 12–14°C, humid. Light rain layer essential — the falls spray is substantial. Waterproof phone pouch for the park.

Phones

T-Mobile and Verizon international plans work fine. WhatsApp is the default messaging app in Argentina — install / test on both phones before departure. Download offline maps of Palermo and Puerto Iguazú.

Iguazú timing note

Late July is peak Argentine winter school break (vacaciones de invierno). Iguazú will be busier than off-season — that's why the plan has you at the park at opening, and at Devil's Throat in the late afternoon when buses have cleared.

Optional add-ons

For Becky's call — any can be slotted in without breaking the plan.

  • A quieter graduation dinner. Don Julio is the famous parrilla — and the wrong sensory environment for Kit (loud, packed, long line outside, tight tables). Better-fitting options for a milestone meal:
    • Casa SaltShaker — puerta cerrada (closed-door) dinner in a host's home, 5-course shared table, intimate by design. The opposite of a packed parrilla.
    • La Brigada — San Telmo parrilla with the same quality meat as Don Julio, half the price, calmer atmosphere.
    • Palo Santo Hotel's restaurant or a concierge-recommended neighborhood spot with a "quiet table, low-stimulation" request at booking. The graduation milestone is the experience together, not the restaurant's prestige.
  • Jardín Japonés — Adjacent to Jardín Botánico on Sunday. Separate paid ticket (~ARS 13,500 non-residents).
  • Escape Buenos Aires — Private bilingual escape room in Caballito. Slot into any free evening.
  • Timbre 4 — Acclaimed director Claudio Tolcachir's independent theater in Boedo. Check timbre4.com for English-subtitled productions in the window.
  • San Antonio de Areco — Full-day gaucho estancia in the pampas. Camino Pampa is the small-group operator. Would replace the Tuesday Recoleta day.
  • Fundación PROA · Penumbra — Dia Art Foundation show (Turrell, Felix Gonzalez-Torres, Agnes Martin) in La Boca. Closes August 2 — could swap into Sunday afternoon for MALBA, or skip.
  • Brazilian side of Iguazú — Adds a different perspective on the falls. Requires a Brazil eVisa for US citizens (~$80, ~72-hour approval, full documentation) — start the application this week if including.
